items.text: After a layoff, COBRA is the letter that finds you. It is not the only option. Losing that job also opened a 60-day Marketplace window, and the subsidy there is based on this year's income, not last year's. honorbrook-insurance.com

After a layoff, COBRA arrives in the mail and feels like the only option. It is worth ten minutes to check whether it is the right one.

COBRA continues the exact plan you had, same network, same deductible progress. What changes is who pays. Your employer was likely covering a large share of that premium; now you pick up all of it, plus an administrative percentage. The plan did not get worse. The bill got honest.

The part people miss: losing job-based coverage also opens a 60-day Special Enrollment Period on the Marketplace. And Marketplace subsidies are calculated on the income you expect this year, which just changed substantially. People who assumed they earn too much to qualify often qualify now, precisely because they were laid off.

Sometimes COBRA still wins. If you are mid-treatment and have met your deductible, starting over on a new plan in October can cost more than the COBRA premium. That is a real calculation, not a slogan.

Run both before the 60 days close. We do that at no cost.

Honorbrook Insurance, Tysons VA. honorbrook-insurance.com
